frequency_question: What proportion of major complex legislative reform packages initiated or accelerated in late-session windows successfully complete all procedural steps and receive presidential signature within 35 days?
membership_rule: Includes any major, multi-title structural reform or infrastructure bill that required bicameral agreement and committee reconciliation, passing both chambers and receiving presidential signature within a 35-day window from final major floor action. Excludes standard continuing resolutions, routine appropriations extensions, and must-pass disaster supplemental bills.

cases.name: TARP / Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008
Continuing Appropriations and Ukraine Supplemental Appropriations Act

provenance_note: claims 35 cases from only 5 named (7.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 5 named; estimated roughly 35 total major structural bills attempted under severe end-of-session time constraints across 15 Congresses.
known_gaps: Excludes minor technical corrections and clean continuing resolutions which have a near 100 percent pass rate under similar timeframes but do not match the structural complexity of comprehensive energy permitting reform.
skeleton: Decomposed into legislative cycles where major structural overhauls were jammed into end-of-year or emergency 35-day windows. Total observed instances in modern polarized Congress meeting this strict timeline: 5 hits out of approximately 35 attempted major structural packages requiring reconciliation.
multiplier: 5 hits / 35 total attempts for major structural reform bills passing within a <=35 day active legislative window.
validity_reason: The procedural rules of Congress remain stable through the current congressional term, after which rules packages are readopted.
